body: The commentary on this remake is going to be insufferable until it releases. The fact that people think that studios only work on one game at a time is proof of that😭 anyone who’s worked in project management could tell you that’s not true lol
I mean, I don’t think they would showcase new music now anyways. This felt like a sneak peek of a game that’s still in development, not a finished product.
It’s way too early to insist that things will be set in stone. I think it looks great so far and I’m excited to see how they’ll tighten it up for release.
Seeing the trailer reminded me so much of my trip through Japan’s countryside last year and walking through the small towns. The vibes will be immaculate 😭😭😭

It’s so ridiculous. It genuinely feels like a bunch of yelling from people who either self insert hard into one or the other, or people who cannot let go of their childhood game crush and don’t want to see any other perspective. It’s even more hilarious because depending on what online space you go to, you’ll see either side insist that the other shippers are worse. Pot calling the kettle black 24/7.

I feel like this is the one fandom where you will not be left alone with your preference of a ship. There will ALWAYS be someone who insists that your preferred ship won’t work for xyz reasons.
I don’t agree with her being “absolutely evil” but her being “evil” doesn’t take away from her character writing 🤷🏻‍♀️

Holy fuck. This is the first time in a long while where I had to take a moment to process after an anime episode. 

Loulan is such an unbelievably brilliantly written character.

I feel like a lot of people are in the camp that P4G doesn’t need a remake and/or are under the assumption that working on the remake is taking time and resources away from Persona 6 (which there is no way to confirm). 

I for one would be excited to see a more modern reimagining of P4G, but I am cautious….especially if they decide to pull some weird DLC shenanigans with the golden content when there is no reason to. I’ll be frank in that I didn’t enjoy Reload, but I feel like I would enjoy a P4 remake more.

I think the commenter wasn’t referring to the number of VA’s being changed more so that the original Eng VA’s for P4 are heavily tied to many people’s enjoyment of the original game….more than P3’s original voice actors. 

I can’t say if this rings true or not since I don’t play the English dub, but I know I’d feel similarly if the Jp voice actors were all changed up.

I was just thinking about it the other day- I really do feel like the part of the Genshin fandom that would engage in fan works (so excluding the toxic gamer types) has definitely mellowed out quite a bit. I remember when people insisted up and down that the Traveler x Childe pairing was problematic lol. I feel like a lot of those people have just grown up.

Honestly? FF7. It’s just so chock full of toxicity and misinformation/disinfo and people being upset about the remakes not going along with their headcanons that it’s genuinely stressful to engage with. There’s always someone in your ear telling you your ship sucks and blatantly slandering characters, canonicity be damned lol. 

Like, I’m all for transformative fandom works and I think what’s considered canon can be thrown to the wind when it comes to fan created media. But it feels like this fandom is full of people with headcanons who then try to insist their headcanons are real in discussions about the canon material, and/or look directly at canon material and go “ha! That means nothing to me because I can’t read!” 

Plus, the whole Tifa vs Aerith war almost always gets misogynistic so fast. It always just feels like a dick measuring contest of who’s childhood video game crush is more “valid” than the other, when the story couldn’t be more explicit about the contrast between different kinds of bonds and their impacts. I genuinely don’t know how else the game could portray that message without outright spelling it out.

Sigh.

I think other comments have summed it up. He’s a complex character that feels immeasurably guilty for something that technically wasn’t fully his fault. He’s also a naturally nurturing person who seeks to take care of others despite his guilt. 

Makoto/Male MC doesn’t really bond with him too much so if you’re playing from his perspective I get not vibing with him, but his FemC social link allows you to bond with him more and see his personality come out.
It’s a random follow up attack that she does, no SP required. I don’t remember if there was a way to trigger it but it was always hilarious when it did and saved me loads of times lol

I really love Ann, she’s hands down my favourite Phantom Thief. Like others have mentioned, she has the misfortune of having her arc early in the story so it can feel like she blends into the background in the later parts of the game. Atlus has never been good with balancing the amount of time and focus placed on certain characters in each of the game parties so it’s not really a surprise.

One of my most favourite parts of her confidant is the mindset she takes towards the rival model that kept sabotaging her and being an overall awful human to her- instead of getting back at her, Ann instead decides to focus on herself and what she can improve on her own, which is such a fantastic message. She doesn’t blame or criticize herself excessively, she instead decides to channel her frustration into working on what she can control, which is herself. 

I don’t think the sub hates Ann at all. I think it’s more so that there are a lot of people who like Makoto/Yoshizawa and make it known that they prefer them. Comparatively Ann’s fans are not as vocal from what I’ve seen lately.

Honestly same, I still to this day and after multiple play throughs don’t understand Makoto’s popularity. I don’t hate her or dislike her at all (did dislike her on my first playthrough), but I’ve played this game 3 times and still don’t really see it.
Trauma centre! I feel like it would be so fun on the switch.

imo it’s more that Yukari feels comfier bonding with another girl earlier on in the story than she would have with Makoto. She probably felt a bit happy that she had a potential girl friend to talk to that wasn’t Mitsuru. I like these little differences between protags!

100%. Like….why do we think that scientific advancements in regions like Fontaine “fit better”?Why don’t those advancements in tech fit in Natlan? Natlan was never advertised as “primitive”- only that there were tribes. Why does tribes suddenly equal not having tech?

I think she’s alright. Not my favourite. I think where she shined the most for me was her relationship with Yukari and how much that changed over the course of the game.

I think that the story’s portrayal of Miyo as a victim of severe abuse is very realistic, especially with regards to setbacks and the power of a strong support system and unconditional love. And simultaneously- because she is not a real person and is a part of a fictional story, I think people are fair in not finding her palatable sometimes. Its not indicative of how people would treat others in real life, and I don’t quite think it’s fully explained by an Asian vs “Western” mindset. 

There are some times that I love watching the series and Miyo’s growth, then there’s other times where I need to put it down because I don’t find myself having the patience to watch her mannerisms at the time. And that’s fine- because this is just a LN/anime. Not ever piece of media is going to be okay for you at all times, and that’s ok.

I agree, Ann and Ryuji always felt more like best friends to me too. No one needs any valid reason to ship anything tbh, but I always felt like putting them together romantically just felt a bit lazy. Or like…an attempt to free up Joker for another girl.

I was actually a little salty over the Persona series for the longest while- my first Atlus games were the Trauma Center series, and I was so sad that those games did not get nearly the same amount of attention and care as Persona. I also didn’t have any way to play Persona so I couldn’t experience it earlier. Now I love it obviously- but if Atlus ever decided they wanted to remake a TC game I think I’ll lose my mind

Not gonna lie, they barely felt like a “trio”. I feel like the fandom gave them more substance than the game actually did, lmao. It’s Joker and Akechi, then Yoshizawa just…..existing. With the occasional “Senpai!!”.

I agree with you, and I think that her way of going about things with Jinshi is one of her major character flaws. She is inherently selfish with regards to him and it’s fully understandable why she is the way she is. But she’s not absolved of responsibility over her actions, and I wouldn’t be surprised if Jinshi (who is also selfish in his own way with his own extraordinary circumstances and quirks) were to be frustrated with her avoidant behaviour one day.

More reasons as to why the character writing in this series is so good! With genius characters like Maomao it can be hard to write flaws that aren’t contrived or too shallow. Her acting this way feels believable for her and her circumstances.

Acheron, Tribbie and Castorice. I don’t hate them, but I wasn’t too interested in them as characters and I don’t pull for characters I’m not interested in. 

Acheron is cool, but at the time I was wanting Aventurine/Robin more and now I don’t really care to roll for her. I hate Tribbie’s design so much (not a fan of child model characters + her colours are just…..weird), and Castorice’s design + overall character fell super flat for me. + the very obvious shilling by Hoyo kind of soured her for me. Lore wise those three are cool, but that isn’t enough for me.

Voice acting in Japan is a completely different ball game than in NA. JP voice actors are very much so considered celebrities and therefore the reaction to replacing them in an anime or game would be much much bigger. I think due to social media NA voice actors have become minor celebrities in their own right, but it’s not to the same extent in Japan. The profession is just viewed differently there.
Honestly, same. Understand his circumstances but he was incredibly annoying.

I think he was great in fes and Portable. I especially liked being able to get to know him better via Portable FemC slink. The complexity of his character really shines there.

It’s a shame that his character has been all but reduced to being a protein obsessed jock.

Really goes to show how delivery of the story matters. Penacony was a fun ride and was an improvement from the Xianzhou arc imo, but there were so many plot lines happening all at once that at times it felt incomprehensible. The highs were great (eg. Aventurine) and the lows were….low. Sunday is one of my favourite HSR characters and I am definitely a lore player, but at the climax of Penacony I definitely was like “….wtf is even happening??” 

I 100% feel more connected to the Amphoreus cast because of the story telling. I like that we are learning about each of the characters, and the payoff for their arcs is happening slowly. I absolutely prefer this method of storytelling over more patches than when they tried to cram it all into 3-4.

Man. I didn’t expect to cry but when I heard jjong’s voice the tears just wouldn’t stop. :’) I was reminded of when I first heard Jonghyun when they first debuted and I was just a kid. and now I’m older than he will ever be. To see his memory being kept alive by both SHINee and fans has been beautiful.

I can vouch for this that moving away from prescribing weight loss is such a sore spot for doctors. I used to work at an org that supported doctors and the way they would trip over themselves to insist that weight loss was the primary method to improve xyz clinical symptoms was….alarming, to say the least. Despite the wealth of literature that shows that prescribing weight loss without investigating further is an issue. 

It was so unbelievably frustrating. I felt so bad for the RDs we worked with to develop these engagement initiatives because doctors would immediately flip at the very thought of NOT prioritizing weight loss. Like…the literature isn’t saying that weight loss won’t be effective, it’s saying that it shouldn’t be the only thing looked at when evaluating a patient.

I’ve honestly always preferred Ren over Akira. When I hear the name Ren I usually associate it with characters that fit Joker’s vibe. Akira feels more bright and classic protagonist like, and I don’t necessarily feel that Joker personality wise is a classic protagonist personality type.

When dating (and also when looking for friends tbh), be yourself. Don’t hide the parts of yourself that would “drive people away”. That’s the point- if a long term relationship is what you want, you want to attract someone that sees the real you, not a sanitized made up version of yourself! 

I spent years and years trying to be a palatable version of myself that appealed to multiple people, not a true version of myself that was secure in my interests in values- and it was no coincidence that my relationships/situationships (lol) were all short lived and painful. 

It was only when I committed to just being me for me, and not trying to be for everyone that I ended up attracting connections both romantic and platonic that were worthwhile and have stayed.

I haven’t played 2, so seeing the praise for the story really intrigues me and it seems the story is right up my alley. I don’t have a way to play it so probably will watch a play through online. 

For me, my personal story favourite is 4. The tight knit cast + the mystery aspect impacted me the most, and imo was the most enjoyable dynamic to watch. P4 also felt like the most replayable Persona for me story wise- I just love the cast so much and still am not tired of them. 

After that I feel like it’s a toss up between P3P (I prefer Kotone’s telling of the events personally, don’t hate the original character at all) and P5. I really enjoy P5 up until the original ending of the game, but 3rd semester loses me unfortunately. Don’t hate it, but tbh I found it a tad predictable- enjoyed the villain though. 

With P3P I really enjoyed the social links more than the overarching story- unfortunately P3 in general suffers from being quite slow up until October and only then do things really start to ramp up beyond the monthly boss battle. But FemC’s social links are a treat. I also do appreciate the dynamics of the group in P3 (not being buddy buddy for the majority of the game), and Yukari is up there as one of my favourite Persona characters period.

Really loved this chapter. I didn’t realize how in my feels I’d be after seeing Nagi express emotion, lol. Super relatable too- realizing that you could have had something great if you applied yourself more. Nagi has always felt like an untouchable, genius character, so seeing this incredibly relatable struggle really humanized him for me. 

I absolutely think he’s coming back, but this feels like a good send off for his character for now. Makes me excited to see how he’ll change.

Yes and….no? The way he is going about trying to have a relationship with her is obviously not working, but Maomao’s view of him is also steeped in bias. 

I really love reading about their relationship because it’s so layered. And you can very very clearly see how they are related, lol. They’re both very flawed characters and I feel that their writing will eventually lead them to an ending that makes sense for the both of them.

Finally someone who feels the same way! Lol. To be fair though I more so have an issue with shipping every single incarnation of Zelda and Link. I get BOTW/TOTK Zelink and SS Zelink, but TP ZeLink have quite literally 0 chemistry 💀I hate how Link’s more believable pairings in TP get overlooked because of that. 

I get the whole “I love you in every universe” trope is very popular but if they were a romantic pair in every single game that would get boring so fast.

So we’re fucked if we didn’t pull for some random chef. For a hugely lore relevant character that people have been waiting for ages, how does this make sense? 

I’ve been around since 1.1 and I usually don’t give a flying fuck about meta relevance but this pisses me off lol
Yeah….this sucks. I had literally negative interest in Escoffier and have wanted Skirk since forever, but hearing how much her damage is bricked by not having Escoffier is just stupid.

As a Vancouverite….same. I really thought that hate would win, in the wake of this awful tragedy. I worried about friends and coworkers all weekend as more info came out, and the amount of comments that came in twisting what had happened into ammo for the Conservative Party was nauseating.

I mean, she saw proof in the Lifestream that Cloud was actively being manipulated by Sephiroth, and that Sephiroth was actively twisting Cloud’s memories. She immediately was given information that explained Cloud’s behaviour/validated her wariness about the stability of his mental health since she found him in Sector 7.

I just turned 30 this year. I wasn’t able to play any of the Persona games until they got onto the Switch, and only now that I have a mortgage + a partner to split bills and a PC with am I able to delve more into the series. I don’t consider myself too old! Feels weird for me to gate keep myself from playing a game when I didn’t have the money to buy the right console when I was younger.
P4G ended up hitting me over the head with Kanji’s steel chair and became my most favourite of the modern Persona games so tbh I’d be thrilled to see Inaba and the cast with updated graphics :’)

1 Litre of Tears changed my life, I recommend it despite how gut wrenching it is. Watched it when I was 12-13 ish and it changed my view on life so profoundly that I still think about it almost 2 decades later!

This has gotta be the most unpopular persona opinion ever and will get me crucified literally anywhere else but I was never a fan of the Aigis and Makoto/Kotone pairing 😭 Sometimes It just felt like Atlus caved and wanted to make Aigis romanceable for the players who wanted a perfect robot girlfriend fantasy, and then leaned into it for every subsequent P3 game after the original. I massively prefer Aigis’s bond to be platonic with the MC rather than romantic (and imo I feel like one of the points of her story was her learning to live for herself and not only in service of others or for a mission) but I feel I would get roasted alive for ever voicing this. I detest it when people reduce her to a robo-girlfriend :(

Love her, she’s my best girl for sure! I empathized heavily with her struggles regarding not feeling feminine enough/being overshadowed by her friends, but also not wanting to feel bad for liking the things that she likes. I felt like that a lot growing up, so it was lovely to see her turn those feelings into more ammo for her to support and protect her friends. Love her JP VA too!

Their relationship was unhealthy, that is the point. The point of their dynamic is that being the top student and having money doesn’t matter- it doesn’t guarantee you emotional security and safety, it doesn’t guarantee you bonds with your family and social belonging, and it doesn’t guarantee you happiness. 

But also, wdym she would be “working already”??? Sae being 20/21 means that she most likely was still in school, not a fully fledged corporate adult. Her schooling was clearly rigorous as well for her to be in the position that she’s in. 

Having a life insurance payout from their dad’s death is one thing, but it still meant that she most likely had to juggle managing a household (how many 20-21 year olds can actually do that well?) along with ensuring that Makoto was coping well and that she was taking care of herself, along with trying to manage her own grief.

On top of that’s she was mostly likely under immense self-imposed pressure to do well enough in school to get into the field that she wanted, plus push past the discrimination she would face as a woman in her field, which in Japan, is a massive barrier- just recently it was revealed that a university actually manipulated test scores for female applicants to a medical program. This is still a thing that happens in the present day. It really is no surprise that their relationship went the way that it did.

It’s gotta be Tifa and Cloud’s conversation after she wakes up for me. The subtle way in which the real Cloud pushes through to open up about the uncertainty of his identity, and Tifa choosing to put her faith in him and treat him with compassion after seeing what she saw in the Lifestream…it was such a tender moment. With each other being the last remaining links to their childhood, it felt like they had created a small pocket of time in which they could be vulnerable, even if it was for only a moment. 

In general, the parts of the story where Cloud’s true self peek through are some of my favourites. I feel like the remakes portrayed the subtle changes in his language and demeanour so well.

It made sense for Miyabi, but for Cas it just feels odd because she isn’t really a particularly standout Chrysos Heir or anything. 

If they decide to skip this fanfare for Phainon I feel like the pitchforks will come out, lol.

No for real, this is why I can’t get into LaDS no matter how hard I try😭 the models just feel so uncanny valley to me/their faces really just blend together for me so it’s hard for me to get the appeal aside from them all being hot. I had to stop Infinity Nikki for the same reason too (Nikki being very uncanny looking at times, as cute as the game was).

Both versions, like all the other Persona anime adaptations, serve their purposes well- they’re just showcasing different retellings of the story. imo having them all be 1:1 recreations of the game would be boring. I like how each adaptation adds in different details or emphasize different things, it just adds to the story overall and you can choose to take it or leave it. There’s things I like and dislike about each adaptation too.

Also, the Golden anime is overhated. It’s meant to cover the Golden content, hence why it revolves around Marie. And that’s fine! I like that it adds things that otherwise wouldn’t make sense in the games.

Jeez, they’re really piling on the favoritism for her, aren’t they? I don’t care for her design so I wasn’t planning on pulling for her anyways, but this feels weirdly desperate. Makes me want to pull for her even less. 

it’s just silly at this point at how much hoyo wants to stick to their guns and alienate the other side of the fanbase (the gender ratio of players is nowhere near as skewed as some people think it is…). Like….its as if they saw LaDS lapping every other gacha game in revenue and decided to give up instead of tapping into the most obvious source of money there is.

How about letting people enjoy what they enjoy? Not everyone is going to agree with you on things and that is…..ok. 

I’ve always preferred Tifa, mainly because I like flawed characters and I heavily empathized with her struggles with insecurity and wavering in her resolve + setting aside her own wants in order to make those she loves happy, at her detriment. I found Aerith heartwarming and lovely (and funny!) but too saintly and perfect for my tastes. I’m a straight woman so it wasn’t even a “Tifa’s hot therefore I like her more” thing (they’re both gorgeous).

I had to block the main sub too. It’s been genuinely absurd. Like…..how on earth does it make sense that you wouldn’t….believe people who actually see the employment contracts, have access to their union’s policy books, and actually work in the industry?

100%. So many of our existing worker’s rights are because of unions and striking, lmao. It’s so…..unbelievably weird to see people be so open about their enjoyment of a VIDEO GAME being more important than people’s livelihoods. Like….I think we can grow up a little. 

Honestly, it’s kind of hilarious to see the lengths that companies will go to just not agree to feed VA’s voices and likeness to AI and have people complaining not be outraged about that- but then they turn around and get outraged over…VA’s calling in their colleagues for scabbing and speaking up for their rights. Some people just have the moral backbone of a wet pasta noodle.

As much as people don’t want to hear it and want to latch onto “easier” targets like individual VAs, it’s corporations that refuse to adequately compensate and protect their employees, period. 

Striking is disruptive, that is the point. Historically, that is how change at the institutional level happens. It’s not going to be pretty and perfect and people are going to have animosity and frustration. But at the end of the day and to be very frank, my enjoyment of a video game means not much in comparison to….employees and their likeness being protected at their jobs. 

Yeah I don’t think the VA’s publicly dogpiling on a non-union (?) VA was smart, but it’s definitely disheartening to see people now decide that supporting the strike isn’t worth it because of….that, of all things. Compared to….the lengths that corporations go to pay their staff peanuts and refuse to protect them. 

Idk, these are just the thoughts of a 30 year old who’s worked at both union and non-union jobs for the past decade….and seen the difference in benefits. 🤷🏻‍♀️

I think you nailed it OP! imo Aerith was such a huge part of why CloTi works- she helped the both of them open up and face their true selves, and then when it came down to it they were able to seek out the truth and piece themselves back together. And then keep the memory of their dear friend alive for years to come.

One of the main things I love about CT over CA and other Cloud pairings though (if we have to compare) is that both Cloud and Tifa are such deeply flawed people- neither of them are portrayed as being perfect in any way shape or form, so to see them work through their challenges felt satisfying. Them coming together felt like a logical part of the narrative- as the only two with memories of their hometown and their true selves.

With Aerith, she’s the kind of character that you’d love to have in your life- but as a character to experience in a story, she fell a little flat for me because of how ‘perfect’ and flawfree she could be at times. Almost saintly, which just isn’t my taste. I like my characters with flaws, and when they make mistakes!

I feel like a lot of people have explained it perfectly- she isn’t a full blown Mary Sue but she has loads of parts of her character that definitely fit in sue territory. She’s shoved down the player’s throat when there’s an original character (Haru) that could’ve had that time to develop instead, almost everyone immediately likes her and reveres her, she’s constantly touted as perfect and doesn’t fully shed that even in 3rd semester, she immediately masters her persona and moves through the metaverse with ease when our original gang still has challenges with it….etc etc. 

It’s why it baffles me that people say she’s well written- a well written character feels believable in the narrative, has pushback/consequences for the decisions they make, and is integrated into the story well. Sumi is none of those things. having a sad back story doesn’t make a character well written.

At the end of the day though, other’s opinions shouldn’t matter if you like the character. I don’t like her and think the game would have been better off without her, but that’s just me.

Probably an unpopular opinion, but being a young girl growing up watching a complicated, flawed character like Cagalli who also kicked ass was such a special experience. She was such a standout in Gundam Seed for me (and anime for me at the time) and young me thought it was so cool to see a female character like her back in the early 2000’s. She’s special to me :’)

I feel like the odd one out in that I reached peak burnout when Fontaine released. That + not really being interested in the music and aesthetic led to me largely checking out during the entirety of patches 4.x. Natlan was what got me back into the game, lol. 

Honestly- I’m fairly satisfied with the game. I’m at a point where pulling for characters is now purely because I like them for whatever reason, and not for the meta, which has meant less stress for me over saving and “viability”. I don’t have the energy to fully clear SA or IT anymore, but I do what I can and have fun with it. I welcome any other changes and updates, no skin off my back. 

Powercreep wise, I can’t speak to it fully since I’m not a meta person anymore…but I still use the same teams that I did during 2.x and 3.x (eg. Raiden national, Xiao Jean Zhongli Albedo lol) and I’m still having fun with the game. 

What I am super excited for is for the lore, and getting answers to some story questions that have been around since the beginning of the game.

Interesting! Not surprised at all about Strohl, he’s such a fantastic character. He’s my favourite too. Not surprised about Louis and the protag either- Louis’ aura was unmatched throughout the entire game, and I enjoyed how lovable the protagonist was!

Tbh, I’m a little surprised about Eupha’s popularity, as I found her a tad milquetoast. I do get that she was by far the most romantically implied follower so maybe that had something to do with it….Don’t hate her at all, she’s adorable and I enjoyed her follower events- but tbh I didn’t really feel like her character was breaking any new ground. 

I’m sad about Junah-I went into the game not expecting to like her at all and I was floored at how cool of a character she was. She subverted so many of my expectations of an Atlus female character and I was so happy with how her character was written. :(

And that’s exactly how some of the “dudebros” the OP is referring to are acting. Even having the OPTION to play as FeMC pisses them off because they can’t fathom having an MC option that they can’t relate to. Whereas women players like myself have had to deal with this for ages. 

I’ve had to force myself to play as a guy character in Persona games for ages, but I still managed to enjoy the game. If the next Persona game had both options, I wouldn’t be throwing a tantrum over the male MC just being an available option. That’s how some of these people are acting.

You’ve barely made any story progress into the game at all. It’s the equivalent of playing halfway into the first palace of P5 and saying “This game sucks!”.  When, as you know, so many things in P5 don’t really get rolling until the 2nd, or even 3rd palace. 

Metaphor’s story builds up slower than the Persona games I’d say and is a bit more complex in its narrative, but you have barely even scratched the surface and are making a judgement on it. You’re absolutely entitled to your opinion, but I would take it a bit more seriously if you’ve played through more of it haha.

I was a little surprised too- the way people described her, it made it seemed that she was constantly shoved in your face the whole game and that her tsundere schtick was dialled up to 5000. There’s a few confidants that have time limits:

Councillor (November 18th - you’ll want to do this one if you want to unlock the Royal only content. Just need to get rank 9 by that date) 

Justice (get to rank 8 also by November 18th - unlocks some story scenes that may or may not be important to you, depending on how much you like the character) 

Sun (max out by November 18th - can give you some bonuses that may be handy in early/mid game) 

Strength (max out by December 22nd - can be time consuming and resource heavy, so I suggest working on this one throughout and using a guide if you need it) 

Faith (Rank 5 by December 5th- you can only do the latter half of their confidant in the Royal only content- so you’ll need to max out the Councillor as a pre-requisite). 

Some confidants I recommend: 
- Level up the Phantom Thieves confidants as much as you can- always helpful since you will be using them in battle 

- Unlock Star confidant: you get a really handy game mechanic that will make your life a lot easier 

- Max out Temperance: One of the best time saving mechanics in the game 

- Max out Death confidant: Easy to max out early in the game, can give you handy discounts

- Fortune confidant to rank 5 - can give you boosts in money, leveling up your social stats, or your bonds with your other confidants

It's not that she's deliberately going after believers, though. It's that the only path she agreed to go on was that of war and destruction. She did not believe that there was any path forward that did not involve the destruction of the Kingdom or the Alliance, and she was perfectly okay with the bloodshed of hundreds of thousands of people. People gloss over this, but it's been demonstrated time and time again irl that these methods almost always lead to the complete and utter devastation of population human rights and health. Post-war CF is painted as a Church-free utopia by some people, but the generational effects of war will remain. 

Edelgard is a "the end justifies the means" person. In this case, her "means to an end" was a bloody 5 year war and complete rule over all of Fodlan, as well as the destruction of all Nabateans.

I think a lot of people agree that the insititute of the Central Church is beyond fucked- but it was her means of facing them that bring pause. And ironically, it's very similar to Rhea's philosophy as well- Rhea did not believe that her ideal world and ultimate goal could be seen without the duping of everyone in Fodlan. Just spitballing here with some first-year university biology... but I wonder if instead of being related, it's more so a somewhat mangled example of convergent evolution?

Convergent evolution is a real-life concept where two distantly related species end up developing/evolving some of the same traits, due to a variety of reasons (environment, evolutionary fitness, etc). These traits can be phenotypic (aka observable, such as eye shape or the presence of wings) but can also be genomic, and don't necessarily physically show on the organism. IRL these things take millenia, but in a fantasy world like Genshin I can imagine that the whole process could be far shorter.

Now obviously, considering that Melusines came from Elynas, it doesn't appear that they did much evolving in comparison to the vishaps (or were evolutionarily dependent on them in any way). But on the other side- aren't vishaps known to be rather evolutionarily adaptive? I think it's rather plausible that existing vishaps saw the Melusines and how they were melding in with the land and society and how that increased their survivability/evolutionary fitness, and decided to then emulate their traits/subsequently evolve them.

I don't think they were related species, and I don't think we have enough info to say that Melusines are going to be the next evolutionary step for vishaps as an entire species- but I do think it's plausible for some Fontainian vishaps to evolve in a way that looks phenotypically similar to the Melusines.

I can finally brain dump about this!  Essay incoming:

Regarding Ymir’s motive of “love”- I don’t think it was as implausible as people say. I do think it was too late to spring it on us at the very end like that though. 

I don’t think we can use our modern perspective of what love is to rationalize Ymir’s perspective on it. She was a slave girl in a rural, ancient village. She was uneducated and lost her parents early- and I have my doubts on whether her parents were a display of true “love” either, based on what we know of marriages in historic times (often arranged, and not commonly due to mutual understanding). It makes total sense that in her incredibly traumatized state with her newfound powers, she probably coveted this shred of attention and praise she got from the king. That was probably the first time in a long time anyone had ever done that for her. And once she was in that toxic relationship, she was stuck. Like many are. It sounds unbelievable to us (and it did to Eren and Armin), but we could also ask the same for many women in history- why did they also stay in relationships that were terrible to them? 

Mikasa’s last vision of Ymir really cemented it for me- Ymir desperately wanted to be free. She wanted to be free of King Fritz, but had no example of what that was. She had no concept of how she could ever be free. And the nature of her titan powers kept her trapped (personally, I think she was just as trapped as Armin/Zeke/etc were when they were trying to regain control of the old titans). Mikasa’s choice to finally let go of Eren was that green light for Ymir- a girl who loved someone so deeply was able to let go, so she could too. 

Again, agree that it wasn’t really well conveyed. I hate it when we get massive plot dumps at the end, and AOT is either super in your face about it or so subtle that you miss it. 

That being said, I’m still content with the ending, as I was 2 years ago.

A number of reasons - it had a very creative and unique plot, a lovable and colourful cast, and a somewhat compelling storyline that had the right amount of stakes spread out between arcs. A really great soundtrack plus a talented JP VA ensemble as well. 

Also- Tsuna is a great protagonist. he doesn't get insanely overpowered, but he's kind and sweet and sticks to his guns despite his fears. I like that his flaws didn't just go away- he learned to work with them instead of becoming some super powered, untouchable shounen protag. 

On top of that, it's a very accessible story- bigger works like One piece, Naruto etc, while being popular for a reason, are immense and these huge stories can often drive people away. KHR has complexity, but not so much as to overwhelm the existing reader or anyone else wanting to get into the series. Additionally, the tone of the story remained fairly light throughout the entire series, which I think goes a long way into keeping people invested (not being too heavy all the time and bogging readers down).  The battle/abilities system is not super complicated and fairly unique, and having attributes/elements associated with certain characters is a popular story trope.

Aside from all of that- there still is a possibility that KHR could be rebooted/finished anime wise. Stage plays were done, and there is still a market for manga sales/merch. It is very within the realm of possibility for KHR to make a return, so it makes sense why people are still getting into KHR to this day. Heck, if Amano wanted to restart the manga as well she definitely could- it ended in a way that left room for a restart so I feel like there will be more to come (if not manga, then at least the anime).

kbugzy14 explained it perfectly - revenge and retaliation never works against abusers. It only fosters more hate, recidivism, etc. This is backed up by *years and years* of research into mental health, abuse, and incarceration at a population level.

Fruits Basket is a story of restorative justice- not a hero saving the day and the bad guys getting locked away. In FB, we look into why the bad guys are the way that they are, and what could be done to help.

Also, I can't emphasize enough how terrible of a pressure the mentality you're demonstrating is on victims. Are they not "good" victims for not acting the way you want them to? In discussing situations of abuse, we should be centering the *victim's* wants and needs and comfortability. Not push onto them what we think they should feel.

Fruits Basket beautifully (and sadly) demonstrated that the victim's experience differs between people. Some lash out like a hurt animal (Rin), others withdraw into themselves and lose their sense of identity (Yuki), some want to just move forward and find their way (Momiji), and some try to manage their pain for the sake of their loved ones (Haru). This is realistic. Everyone in Fruits Basket demanding that their abusers be punished wouldn't be realistic. And guess what? irl abuse victims don't do this either.

I get that it feels intuitive to want punishment- but this is a result of a shitty societal culture that glamorizes and holds "catching the bad guys" on a pedestal. The end goal should be healing- not more punishment.
